transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come see me?

I... well, I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me. It's usually through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it's completely turned off. It's the board members, mostly, or some of the senior staff, and they're always saying I'm ruining the company. It sounds so incredibly clear that I actually answer them back before I realize no one else in the room heard a thing. Which reminds me, I need to look into changing the phone system at the office. We switched to this new VoIP provider last quarter and the call quality is just abysmal. I told the IT director it was a mistake, but he insisted it would save us money. You know how it is, everyone's always trying to cut costs, but sometimes you just get what you pay for. I think I'll have my assistant draft an email about it this afternoon.
How long have you been hearing these voices or conversations about you? When did this first start?

Well, the voices from the walls, and the ones coming through the phone... it's been happening for about the past three months. It started right around the end of the last quarter, actually. Which is always a critical time for us, but this year was especially chaotic because our lead accountant decided to just retire out of nowhere. Just packed up his desk on a Tuesday and moved to Florida. We had to use this temp agency to fill the gap, and let me tell you, the people they sent over were completely incompetent. One of them didn't even know how to use basic Excel macros. I ended up having to sit there and show him how to format a simple pivot table, which is absolutely ridiculous for a contractor billing at eighty dollars an hour. I really need to have a word with HR about our vendor contracts. We waste so much money on these useless staffing agencies when we could just be recruiting directly from the university job fairs. I should probably add that to the agenda for Monday's executive meeting...

When you hear these voices coming through the walls or your phone, do you believe they are actually real people talking to you, or do you recognize that something unusual is happening even though the voices sound completely real?

I... I don't really know how to answer that. I mean, they sound completely real to me. It sounds exactly like Richard from the board, and he's always whispering about me anyway. He never liked that I didn't finish my degree, you know. He actually brought it up at the charity gala last year, right in front of the catering staff! 

Which, by the way, those caterers were just awful. The salmon was completely dry. I told my event coordinator—Sarah, her name is—I said, 'Sarah, if you ever book them again, you're fired.' Good help is just impossible to find right now. Everyone wants a massive salary but nobody wants to actually ensure the food is edible. I ended up having to eat the vegetarian option that night, and it was just a plate of soggy eggplant. I absolutely despise eggplant. I really need to remember to have Sarah update my dietary preferences file for all future corporate events... if she hasn't already messed that up, too.

When you hear Richard's voice coming through the walls or your phone, do you think he's actually physically there speaking, or do you think something else might be going on—like maybe your mind is playing tricks on you?

I mean, I don't know if he's physically standing right there behind the drywall. But it's his voice. It's Richard. Why would my mind play tricks on me? I'm not the one playing tricks, he is. He's always been sneaky like that. Just last month, I caught him trying to reorganize the parking assignments without running it by me first. He tried to give my spot—the one right by the east entrance—to the new VP of Marketing. Can you believe that? 

I had to march down to facilities and have a complete fit about it. The facilities manager, Tom, he's been there for twenty years and he still can't seem to get the snow removal right in the winter. Last February, I almost ruined a brand new pair of Prada pumps because they hadn't salted the walkway properly. I told him, 'Tom, if I slip and break my ankle, the lawsuit will cost more than your entire department's budget.' Honestly, the incompetence is just staggering. I should probably have Sarah look into finding a new facilities management company. I think there was a brochure on my desk about one, but the cleaning crew probably threw it away. They always throw away my important papers. I need to leave a sticky note on my monitor about that...

When you think about these voices coming through the walls and phone over these past three months, have you ever wondered if maybe they might not be real, or do you remain pretty convinced that Richard and the others are actually communicating with you?

Well, I'm absolutely convinced it's them. I mean, I hear them so clearly. It's usually the board members, or sometimes the staff, and they're always saying I'm ruining the company. It comes right through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it's completely turned off! It's so loud and real that I actually talk back to them. I'll be sitting there answering them before I even realize that nobody else in the room heard a thing. 

Speaking of the conference room, the chairs in there are an absolute disaster. We spent thousands of dollars upgrading the upholstery last year, and they went with this awful synthetic leather that just traps the heat. You sit in a three-hour strategy meeting and by the end of it, everyone's completely miserable. I specifically told the interior designer—what was her name, Chloe?—I said, 'Chloe, we need breathable fabrics.' But she was too obsessed with this minimalist aesthetic to listen to basic common sense. She actually tried to convince me to replace the mahogany table with a glass one. Can you imagine the smudges? We'd have to have the cleaning crew in there every ten minutes, and like I said, they're already throwing away my important papers. Honestly, if I don't micromanage every single detail, the whole place would just fall apart. I should probably have Sarah order some new fabric swatches for those chairs...

If I told you that Richard wasn't actually behind the walls or on your phone, and that these voices might be coming from your own mind rather than from real people, how would you react to that idea? Would that make sense to you at all, or does that seem completely wrong?

That... that just seems completely wrong. I mean, why would my mind make up Richard's voice? It's his voice, I know his voice, I've listened to him drone on for years. If my mind was going to make up a voice, it certainly wouldn't be his. I'd pick someone with a much more pleasant tone, like maybe a British accent. I love British accents. 

Actually, I was just looking at booking a trip to London for the holidays. I haven't been in ages. The last time I went, I stayed at this gorgeous hotel in Mayfair, but the concierge was completely useless. I asked for tickets to a specific show, and he tried to get me into some dreadful avant-garde play instead. I told him, 'I am not sitting through three hours of interpretive dance.' I ended up having to call my assistant back in the States—this was before Sarah, of course, this was when I had Jessica—and I had to have Jessica sort it out from across the ocean. Jessica was actually quite good at her job, but she left to go to law school. I always told her she'd make a terrible lawyer, she was far too agreeable. You can't be agreeable in law, just like you can't be agreeable in business. If I were agreeable, Richard and the board would have pushed me out years ago. They're always trying to find a way to get rid of me, which is why he's always whispering about me through the walls.

Over these three months, have you ever had even a moment of doubt where you thought, 'Maybe this isn't really Richard, maybe something else is happening'? Or has it always felt completely certain to you that it's actually him?

No, I've never doubted it. Not for a second. It's Richard. It's always Richard. I know his voice, I know his cadence, I know exactly how he clears his throat before he's about to say something completely undermining. Why would I doubt it? It's so obviously him. 

Just like it's obviously him who keeps messing with the thermostat in my office. I swear, I come in every morning and it's set to 68 degrees. 68! I'm practically shivering at my desk. I told Sarah to put a lock box over it, but apparently, building management won't allow it because of some ridiculous fire code. Fire code! As if a piece of plastic over a thermostat is going to burn the building down. I had half a mind to call the fire marshal myself and ask him to explain the logic, but honestly, dealing with city officials is just exhausting. I had to deal with zoning last year when we wanted to expand the employee cafeteria, and the paperwork alone took six months. Six months just to knock down a wall and add an espresso bar! And then the espresso machine they bought was this cheap Italian knockoff that breaks down every other week. I told them to get a La Marzocco, but no one ever listens to me. They just whisper about me instead.

Despite hearing these voices from Richard and others over the past three months, have you been able to keep working and performing your job responsibilities at your normal level, or have these experiences made it difficult for you to do your work?

Well, I suppose... I mean, I'm trying to work, but it's gotten incredibly difficult to keep up. I'm just not reliably able to run the division right now, or even make basic executive decisions. It's like my brain is too crowded. The senior staff have actually started quietly taking over work that I used to handle myself, which is probably exactly what Richard wants. 

Speaking of the senior staff, Greg from accounting has been wearing these absolutely hideous ties lately. I don't know who told him that mustard yellow and teal were a good combination, but it's completely distracting. I tried to bring it up at the last quarterly review, but everyone just stared at me. You'd think at a company of our caliber, there would be some sort of dress code enforcement. I remember when we instituted casual Fridays back in 2018, it was a complete disaster. People were showing up in flip-flops! Flip-flops in a corporate office! I had to send out a company-wide memo detailing the difference between 'business casual' and 'beach attire.' 

But yes, even at home, it's... it's falling apart. My husband has had to take over almost all the household responsibilities. I just leave things unfinished, or I don't even start them at all. I was supposed to organize the pantry last weekend, but I just stood there staring at the canned goods for an hour. We buy this specific brand of organic crushed tomatoes, and the label changed. They used to have this lovely rustic font, and now it's this sterile, modern block lettering. It just completely threw me off. Why do companies feel the need to rebrand when they already have a perfectly good design? It's just like when the city redesigned the parking meters downtown. Now you have to use an app, and half the time the app crashes right when you're trying to pay, and then you get a ticket anyway. I have three unpaid parking tickets sitting on my kitchen counter right now because I just can't bring myself to deal with the app.

I notice you jump from topic to topic quite a bit when you're talking—like from the voices you're hearing to details about office furniture or parking tickets. Do you find it hard to stay focused on one thing, or does your mind just naturally work that way?

I don't... I haven't really noticed that I do that. I just think my mind naturally works faster than other people's. You have to be able to see all the moving parts when you're an executive, so my brain just connects things. It's like a high-performance engine. 

Speaking of engines, my husband actually bought a vintage Porsche last month. A completely ridiculous mid-life crisis purchase, obviously. And he bought it on a Tuesday. Who buys a sports car on a Tuesday afternoon? The dealership is right off the interstate, right next to that enormous billboard for the personal injury lawyer—you know the one, with the guy pointing directly at the highway? I always feel like he's accusing me of something when I drive past. 

Anyway, the salesman who sold him the car apparently chewed gum the entire time they were doing the paperwork. Just smacking his lips. I told my husband he should have walked away right then and there. I absolutely cannot tolerate open-mouth chewing. We had a vendor once, a packaging supplier for our premium line, who chewed a piece of peppermint gum through his entire pitch. I didn't even look at his samples, I just had my assistant show him the door. You can tell everything you need to know about a person's business ethics by their manners. If you can't respect a boardroom, how are you going to respect a supply chain?

Over these past three months, have you noticed that you're less interested in things you used to enjoy, or that you just don't feel like doing things even when you know you should? Like, do you find yourself not caring as much about things, or feeling kind of empty or flat emotionally?

I suppose that's true. I just don't feel much of anything lately. I used to be the person driving every single idea, you know? I was always the one calling people after our new location openings, full of energy, making sure everything went perfectly. But now... now I can just sit at my desk for hours, just staring at the daily agenda. 

And the agendas are printed on this awful, flimsy paper now. We used to use a heavy cardstock, a nice eggshell white, but procurement switched to this recycled nonsense to save three cents a sheet. It completely bleeds through if you use a fountain pen. I only use fountain pens, specifically Montblanc. My father gave me a Montblanc when I got my first executive position. He had it engraved, but the engraver misspelled my middle name. Can you imagine? You pay hundreds of dollars for a luxury item and they put an 'e' instead of an 'a'. It's just sheer incompetence. It's exactly why I don't trust local vendors for corporate gifting anymore. We used a local bakery for holiday baskets one year and half the shortbread arrived crumbled into dust. 

But anyway, yes, I just stare at the paper. I barely even speak to my staff anymore, or my husband for that matter. He's been trying to get me to go to this couples' cooking class with him. A cooking class! As if we don't have a perfectly good private chef. The chef makes this incredible sea bass, though last week he put way too much caper sauce on it. Capers are so overpowering. They taste like little salty pebbles. I read somewhere that capers are actually unripened flower buds. Why are we eating unripened flowers? It seems so impatient. Just wait for the flower to bloom! The botanical gardens downtown have the most beautiful orchids right now, or at least they did before the city slashed their funding. 

So yes, I just feel almost nothing about the work I used to love. It's just... flat.

Over these past three months when the voices started, have you experienced any periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

No... no, I haven't had anything like that. I actually feel like I'm moving through molasses most of the time. Energetic is the last word I would use. I sleep exactly the same amount I always have, though the quality of sleep is terrible because of the sheets. We bought these Egyptian cotton sheets from a boutique in Milan—well, they claimed they were from Milan, but the shipping label clearly said they came from a warehouse in New Jersey. New Jersey! I should have known better. The toll roads in New Jersey are an absolute nightmare. You can't drive five miles without throwing quarters into a basket. Who carries quarters anymore? 

It's completely archaic. Everything should be digital now. Like those smart refrigerators. My sister bought one that supposedly tells you when your milk is going bad, but it just kept connecting to her Bluetooth speaker and playing jazz music at three in the morning. Jazz is so unpredictable. I prefer classical. Bach. There's a structure to it, an order. 

But no, I haven't felt unusually energetic at all. If anything, I'm just exhausted.

During these past three months when you've been hearing the voices, have you ever felt like you had special abilities or insights that others didn't have, or felt like you were particularly important or powerful in some way?

No, I wouldn't say that. I'm exactly who I've always been. I mean, I'm a CEO, so obviously I have a certain level of... authority, and I make decisions that impact hundreds of employees, but that's just my job. It's not a special ability, it's just years of hard work and strategic planning. 

Strategic planning is actually something we've been struggling with lately because our VP of Operations keeps insisting on using these new agile frameworks. Agile! It's just a buzzword they teach in business seminars so consultants can charge a thousand dollars an hour. We had a consultant come in last year who wore these ridiculous neon green socks with his suit. Neon green. I couldn't focus on a single word he was saying about synergy or deliverables because all I could see were his ankles flashing under the conference table. 

It's completely unprofessional. Professionalism is dead, honestly. I went to the bank last week to handle a wire transfer for a new property acquisition, and the teller was chewing on a pen cap while she was typing. A plastic pen cap. And it was one of those cheap ballpoint pens that leave little globs of ink on the paper. I only use Montblanc, as I mentioned before. The ink flows so smoothly, like... like water over river stones. We went to a river house once for a corporate retreat. The mosquitoes were the size of small birds. My assistant got bit right on the eyelid and it swelled up so much she couldn't read the quarterly reports. 

But no, I don't feel like I have special powers or anything. I'm just a business owner trying to keep things running.

When these voices first started three months ago, did it happen suddenly one day, or did it come on gradually over a period of weeks? And was there any point where you felt completely confused about what was real and what wasn't?

I'm not entirely sure how it started, to be honest. It wasn't like a switch flipped. It was more like... well, it was gradual, I suppose. I didn't wake up one morning and suddenly hear them. It was just a slow build. I didn't feel confused about reality, though. I've always had a very firm grasp on reality. You have to, in my position. If you lose your grip on reality in the corporate world, they eat you alive. 

It's like that hostile takeover attempt we dealt with two years ago. The competing firm tried to quietly buy up shares through shell companies. Shell companies! They named one of them 'Blue Horizon Holdings.' Such an uninspired name. If you're going to create a fake company, at least put some effort into the branding. I hired a branding agency once for our rebrand, and they spent three weeks just deciding between two shades of navy blue for our logo. Three weeks! And they charged us a retainer the whole time. They called one shade 'Midnight Depth' and the other 'Oceanic Authority.' It was absurd. I ended up just pointing at a Pantone swatch and telling them to use that. 

Pantone is fascinating, really. The way they categorize every possible color with a number. It's so organized. I wish my closet was organized like that. My dry cleaner keeps mixing up my silk blouses. Last week, I got back a blouse that belonged to someone named Brenda. Who wears a ruffled magenta blouse? It looked like a deflated balloon. I would never wear magenta. It completely washes out my complexion. 

But no, I never felt confused about what was real. I just... started hearing them over time.

Before these voices started three months ago, have you ever had any similar experiences with hearing voices or seeing things that others couldn't see? Or have you ever been hospitalized for any psychiatric or mental health reasons in the past?

No, never. I've never been in a hospital for anything mental, and I certainly didn't hear things before this year. I don't really like hospitals at all, to be honest. The fluorescent lighting is so incredibly unflattering. We actually just retrofitted our entire corporate headquarters with warm-toned LED bulbs because the old fluorescents were giving everyone a headache. Well, that, and they hummed. Just this constant, low-level buzzing sound. It drove my executive assistant absolutely crazy. 

He actually threatened to quit over it, which I couldn't allow because finding good help is impossible these days. Everyone just wants a four-day work week and a standing desk. I tried a standing desk for a week and my calves were absolutely screaming. I had to book an emergency session with my massage therapist, Sven. Sven has these massive hands, like... like bear paws, but he's surprisingly gentle. He told me I carry all my stress in my left shoulder. Which makes perfect sense, because I'm always holding my phone to my left ear while I'm typing on my laptop. I really need to start using a headset, but they always mess up my hair. I get blowouts twice a week and I'm not going to ruin that for a piece of plastic. 

But no, to answer your question, nothing like this in the past. Never hospitalized.

Looking back over your entire life before these three months—even going back to childhood or your teenage years—have you ever had periods where you felt disconnected from reality, or where your thinking felt really confused or disorganized, even if it didn't involve hearing voices?

No, I can't say I ever felt disconnected or confused like that. My thinking has always been incredibly sharp, even when I was a kid. I was the one organizing the neighborhood lemonade stands, calculating our little profit margins when I was twelve. Lemons were so much cheaper back then, too. Now you go to the grocery store and they want two dollars for a single organic lemon. It's absolute extortion. 

I actually tried growing my own Meyer lemon tree on my terrace last spring, but the wind up on the penthouse level is just too brutal for citrus. It snapped the main branch right in half during a storm in October. That storm was a complete nightmare for the city's grid, by the way. We lost power at the office for six hours, and the backup generators didn't kick in because the property manager forgot to schedule the quarterly maintenance. I was furious. I had him on the phone in the dark, and I said, "What exactly are we paying you management fees for?" 

Management fees are such a racket anyway. It's like paying someone an exorbitant amount of money just to exist in your general vicinity. Kind of like my ex-husband's divorce lawyer... just sitting there in mediation, billing by the minute while doing absolutely nothing. His tie was always slightly crooked, too. Just half an inch to the left. It drove me insane. I wanted to reach across the table and fix it, but my own lawyer told me not to engage. 

But anyway, no. I've always been very clear-headed and focused. Never disorganized.

Before these three months, going all the way back—was there ever a time in your life, even just a few weeks or months, where you noticed your thinking became harder to follow or where people around you seemed confused by what you were saying?

No, never. People have always understood me perfectly fine. I'm a very effective communicator, honestly. You have to be in my role. If people are confused by what you're saying, they don't execute the strategy correctly. And execution is everything. It's like... it's like when we tried to launch that new software platform last year. The developers were in a completely different time zone, somewhere in Eastern Europe, I think. 

Trying to coordinate those Zoom calls was just a logistical nightmare. I'd be up at 4:00 AM in my silk pajamas, drinking espresso just to talk to them before their workday ended. Espresso is terrible for my stomach, by the way. My gastroenterologist told me to switch to matcha, but matcha tastes like freshly mown grass. I tried putting almond milk in it, but then it just tastes like creamy grass. 

Anyway, the lead developer, this guy named Yuri, he had this incredibly thick accent, and he kept using all this technical jargon that half my board didn't understand. I had to translate everything he said into actionable business metrics. That's what I do. I make things clear for people. If anything, I'm the one who has to untangle other people's confused thinking. 

Like my sister. She's always all over the place. She called me last week in tears because her golden retriever ate a sock. I told her, "Just take the dog to the vet, don't call me crying about it." But she's always been dramatic like that. She wanted to be an actress when we were teenagers. She actually auditioned for a commercial once, for some sort of anti-dandruff shampoo, but they told her she had too much hair. How can you have too much hair? 

But to your point, no. My thinking has always been very easy to follow. I've never had a problem with it.

You mentioned the voices started about three months ago, and that your work performance has really declined recently. Looking back to before these three months—say, last spring or early summer—were you functioning normally at work, at home with your husband, and in your life generally? Or had things already been falling apart before the voices started?

Well, no, it wasn't just three months ago that things started getting difficult. Honestly, it's been building for about two years and four months. That's when the company expansion happened and they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. It was supposed to be this huge career milestone, right? Blending corporate strategy with fine art acquisitions. 

We were supposed to curate these massive installations for the lobbies of our new commercial properties. I spent three weeks just interviewing art consultants in Paris. Paris is absolutely exhausting in the summer, by the way. The heat just radiates off the pavement, and no one believes in air conditioning. I stayed at this boutique hotel in the Marais, and the AC unit was literally the size of a shoebox. It just weakly blew lukewarm air at my feet while I tried to sleep. 

And the croissants! Everyone talks about the croissants, but honestly, they're so flaky that you end up with crumbs all over your silk blouses. I ruined a perfectly good Chanel top because a piece of butter just melted right into the fabric. I had to take it to this specialty dry cleaner in New York who charges a hundred dollars just to look at a garment. He's this tiny Italian man who yells at you if you use the wrong hangers at home. Wire hangers are a cardinal sin to him, which I suppose I understand. They really do ruin the shoulder line of a good jacket. 

But anyway, yes, the stress of that new division... that's when things really started unraveling. Two years and four months ago. It's just been a slow decline since then, long before the voices started.

Going back over those two years and four months since the expansion—before the voices started—did you ever have a stretch of time, maybe weeks or a month or two, where you felt like you were operating at a much higher level than usual? Like needing much less sleep than normal but still feeling energized, or having so many ideas and plans that your thoughts felt like they were racing ahead of you?

No, I never felt like that. I've always needed my sleep. If I don't get at least seven hours, I'm absolutely useless the next day. I actually bought this incredibly expensive sleep tracking ring last year to monitor my REM cycles. It's supposed to give you a "readiness score" every morning, but honestly, half the time I think it's just making numbers up. 

One morning it told me my readiness was at 98%, and I felt like I had been hit by a truck. I had this awful tension headache right behind my eyes. I get those sometimes when the barometric pressure drops suddenly. My acupuncturist says it's stagnant liver Qi, but I think it's just the weather. Have you noticed how erratic the weather has been lately? We had that random 70-degree day in January, and all the cherry blossoms started blooming early, and then they all froze and died two days later when it snowed. 

It was so depressing looking at those dead little brown flowers on my walk to the office. I usually walk through the park on my way in—it's supposed to be good for your mental health, grounding yourself with nature or whatever. But there are so many aggressive pigeons in that park. One actually swooped down and hit my assistant in the head last week. He dropped my oat milk latte right on the sidewalk. 

Oat milk is getting so expensive, too. I don't understand how they justify the upcharge when oats are literally one of the cheapest crops on the planet. It's completely illogical. 

But no, I've never had racing thoughts or anything like that. Just my normal, steady pace.

In these past two years and four months since the expansion started, was there ever a specific time—maybe a few weeks or a month—where you found yourself sleeping only 3 or 4 hours a night but still felt completely rested and energized the next day, even though that's very different from your normal 7 hours?

No, I already told you, I need my sleep. If I don't get seven hours, I can't function. Three or four hours? I'd be a zombie. I'd never be able to run my division like that. You need a clear head for acquisitions. 

Speaking of acquisitions, we just bought this massive bronze sculpture for the Chicago lobby. It's supposed to represent "synergy," but honestly, it just looks like a giant pretzel. The shipping logistics were a nightmare. We had to hire a specialized flatbed truck, and they had to close down two blocks of downtown Chicago at 3:00 AM just to crane it into the building. 

Chicago is so windy, too. They call it the Windy City for a reason, obviously. I lost a perfectly good silk scarf there once. The wind just whipped it right off my neck while I was walking down the Magnificent Mile. It was vintage Hermès, too. My husband bought it for me for our tenth anniversary. We went to this little bistro in the West Village to celebrate, and they served the most incredible duck confit. 

Duck is so hard to cook right, don't you think? Most places overcook it and it gets all rubbery, but this was perfect. The skin was so crispy. My husband tried to make duck at home once for Valentine's Day. He completely ruined my favorite copper pan. He left it soaking in the sink for three days because he didn't know how to clean it without scratching the finish. Copper pans are so high maintenance. You have to use that special paste to keep them shiny, otherwise they just turn brown and look terrible hanging on the pot rack. 

But no, I've never had a time where I only slept three hours and felt fine. That's just not how my body works.

When you're sitting alone and thinking to yourself—not hearing the voices, just your own thoughts—do your thoughts flow normally and make sense to you, or do you find that your own thinking feels jumbled or hard to follow?

Well, no, my thoughts are perfectly fine. They flow just how they always have. I mean, I have a lot to think about, obviously, running the division and everything. It takes a lot of mental organization to keep all the projects straight. 

I actually use this color-coded filing system for all my physical documents. Blue folders are for domestic acquisitions, red are for international, and green are for structural assessments. I buy the folders in bulk from this little office supply store near my house. It's one of those old-school places that still sells fountain pens and actual ink wells. I bought a fountain pen there once, a really beautiful Montblanc, but I stopped using it because the ink kept staining my fingers. 

It's impossible to get black ink out of a good manicure. I get a gel manicure every two weeks—always a pale, neutral pink, because it looks the most professional. My manicurist, Elena, she's wonderful, but she's always trying to talk me into getting nail art. Little rhinestones or painted flowers. I have to tell her every time, "Elena, I am a chief executive. I cannot sit in a boardroom with the board of directors with little daisies painted on my thumbs." 

She means well, though. She just had a baby, actually. A little boy. She showed me pictures last time I was in, and he was wearing the most ridiculous tiny tuxedo onesie. I don't understand why people dress infants in formal wear. They just spit up on it anyway. 

But my thoughts? No, they aren't jumbled at all. They make perfect sense to me.

We lost power at the office for six hours, and the backup generators didn't kick in because the property manager forgot to schedule the quarterly maintenance. I was furious. It's like... it's like when we tried to launch that new software platform last year. The developers were in a completely different time zone, somewhere in Eastern Europe, I think. 

Trying to coordinate those Zoom calls was just a logistical nightmare. I'd be up at 4:00 AM in my silk pajamas, drinking espresso just to talk to them before their workday ended. Espresso is terrible for my stomach, by the way. My gastroenterologist told me to switch to matcha, but matcha tastes like freshly mown grass. I tried putting almond milk in it, but then it just tastes like creamy grass. 

Anyway, the lead developer, this guy named Yuri, he had this incredibly thick accent, and he kept using all this technical jargon that half my board didn't understand. Well, no, it wasn't just three months ago that things started getting difficult. Honestly, it's been building for about two years and four months. Blending corporate strategy with fine art acquisitions. 

We were supposed to curate these massive installations for the lobbies of our new commercial properties. I spent three weeks just interviewing art consultants in Paris. Paris is absolutely exhausting in the summer, by the way. The heat just radiates off the pavement, and no one believes in air conditioning. I stayed at this boutique hotel in the Marais, and the AC unit was literally the size of a shoebox. It just weakly blew lukewarm air at my feet while I tried to sleep. 

And the croissants! Everyone talks about the croissants, but honestly, they're so flaky that you end up with crumbs all over your silk blouses. I ruined a perfectly good Chanel top because a piece of butter just melted right into the fabric. I had to take it to this specialty dry cleaner in New York who charges a hundred dollars just to look at a garment. He's this tiny Italian man who yells at you if you use the wrong hangers at home. Wire hangers are a cardinal sin to him, which I suppose I understand. They really do ruin the shoulder line of a good jacket. 

But anyway, yes, the stress of that new division... that's when things really started unraveling. Two years and four months ago. It's just been a slow decline since then, long before the voices started.

patient.answer:
No, I never felt like that. I've always needed my sleep. If I don't get at least seven hours, I'm absolutely useless the next day. I actually bought this incredibly expensive sleep tracking ring last year to monitor my REM cycles. It's supposed to give you a "readiness score" every morning, but honestly, half the time I think it's just making numbers up. 

One morning it told me my readiness was at 98%, and I felt like I had been hit by a truck. I had this awful tension headache right behind my eyes. I get those sometimes when the barometric pressure drops suddenly. My acupuncturist says it's stagnant liver Qi, but I think it's just the weather. Have you noticed how erratic the weather has been lately? We had that random 70-degree day in January, and all the cherry blossoms started blooming early, and then they all froze and died two days later when it snowed. 

It was so depressing looking at those dead little brown flowers on my walk to the office. I usually walk through the park on my way in—it's supposed to be good for your mental health, grounding yourself with nature or whatever. But there are so many aggressive pigeons in that park. One actually swooped down and hit my assistant in the head last week. He dropped my oat milk latte right on the sidewalk. 

Oat milk is getting so expensive, too. I don't understand how they justify the upcharge when oats are literally one of the cheapest crops on the planet. It's completely illogical. 

But no, I've never had racing thoughts or anything like that. Just my normal, steady pace.

patient.answer:
No, I already told you, I need my sleep. If I don't get seven hours, I can't function. Three or four hours? I'd be a zombie. I'd never be able to run my division like that. You need a clear head for acquisitions. 

Speaking of acquisitions, we just bought this massive bronze sculpture for the Chicago lobby. It's supposed to represent "synergy," but honestly, it just looks like a giant pretzel. The shipping logistics were a nightmare. We had to hire a specialized flatbed truck, and they had to close down two blocks of downtown Chicago at 3:00 AM just to crane it into the building. 

Chicago is so windy, too. They call it the Windy City for a reason, obviously. I lost a perfectly good silk scarf there once. The wind just whipped it right off my neck while I was walking down the Magnificent Mile. It was vintage Hermès, too. My husband bought it for me for our tenth anniversary. We went to this little bistro in the West Village to celebrate, and they served the most incredible duck confit. 

Duck is so hard to cook right, don't you think? Most places overcook it and it gets all rubbery, but this was perfect. The skin was so crispy. My husband tried to make duck at home once for Valentine's Day. He completely ruined my favorite copper pan. He left it soaking in the sink for three days because he didn't know how to clean it without scratching the finish. Copper pans are so high maintenance. You have to use that special paste to keep them shiny, otherwise they just turn brown and look terrible hanging on the pot rack. 

But no, I've never had a time where I only slept three hours and felt fine. That's just not how my body works.

Well, no, my thoughts are perfectly fine. They flow just how they always have. I mean, I have a lot to think about, obviously, running the division and everything. It takes a lot of mental organization to keep all the projects straight. 

I actually use this color-coded filing system for all my physical documents. Blue folders are for domestic acquisitions, red are for international, and green are for structural assessments. I buy the folders in bulk from this little office supply store near my house. It's one of those old-school places that still sells fountain pens and actual ink wells. I bought a fountain pen there once, a really beautiful Montblanc, but I stopped using it because the ink kept staining my fingers. 

It's impossible to get black ink out of a good manicure. I get a gel manicure every two weeks—always a pale, neutral pink, because it looks the most professional. My manicurist, Elena, she's wonderful, but she's always trying to talk me into getting nail art. Little rhinestones or painted flowers. I have to tell her every time, "Elena, I am a chief executive. I cannot sit in a boardroom with the board of directors with little daisies painted on my thumbs." 

She means well, though. She just had a baby, actually. A little boy. She showed me pictures last time I was in, and he was wearing the most ridiculous tiny tuxedo onesie. I don't understand why people dress infants in formal wear. They just spit up on it anyway. 

But my thoughts? No, they aren't jumbled at all. They make perfect sense to me.
